_doc: Disposition store for the open-question register (DIRECTOR_RULING_NO_QUESTION_LEFT_UNANSWERED 2026-07-28, deliverables 1+2). The QUESTION SET is NOT stored here -- it is DERIVED from primary state (the ruling bodies) by background/open_question_register.py, so it can never silently omit a real question. This file holds ONLY the human judgement: for each question_key, its disposition. A question with NO entry here is 'open' (silent) and BLOCKS archival of its ruling. Statuses: answered|unknown|not_measurable|wrong CLOSE a question (unblock archival); 'carried' is NON-SILENT (has a reason) but UNANSWERED, so it still blocks. Keys are stable 12-char ids (see question_key()).

0d7f5e74b25b.question: Verified-commit forgeability: if the worker holds no API-capable token, is 'verified commit + [DIRECTOR-RULING] marker' a property the worker CANNOT forge? If yes propose a bridge-staged second channel R15-proven both ways; if no say why with evidence.
0d7f5e74b25b.disposition: ANSWERED (2026-07-28, NO -- and the premise is FALSE in this environment; evidence, not assertion). The conditional's antecedent ('the worker holds no API-capable token') does NOT hold here, so 'verified commit + marker' is NOT a non-forgeable property. Evidence, all run this session: (1) `gh auth status` -> logged in as 21bcarlisle-arch with token `gho_...`, scopes include `repo` + `workflow`. (2) The token REACHES the API: `gh api user` -> `21bcarlisle-arch`; `gh api repos/21bcarlisle-arch/synthetic-enterprise/contents/CLAUDE.md?ref=main` -> returns the file (name+sha) -- the SAME endpoint a PUT would hit to create a verified commit. (3) Repo permissions for that token: `{admin:true, maintain:true, push:true, triage:true, pull:true}`. (4) The token lives in `/home/rich/.config/gh/hosts.yml` (owner rich, mode 0600) and `whoami`=rich -- the SAME OS user under which autonomous_runner spawns `claude -p` worker turns, so a worker turn shares it (GH_TOKEN unset in env, but `gh` reads hosts.yml directly). => The worker can call `PUT /repos/.../contents/...` with this token; GitHub marks the resulting commit 'Verified' (signed by GitHub's own key on the token-holder's behalf) carrying ANY message including `[DIRECTOR-RULING]`. The 'Verified' badge certifies 'GitHub authenticated the token holder', NOT 'the director authored this' -- and the worker holds that token. Corollary: the weaker author-name channel (`is_valid_advisor_ruling`, keyed on `21bcarlisle-arch`) is a fortiori forgeable -- that IS already the worker's push identity (its own docstring flags this as defence-in-depth only). THEREFORE: a bridge-staged gate-open keyed on 'verified commit + marker' would be FORGEABLE -> under R15 it is a control that CANNOT FAIL on its own defect (the worker forging its own release) = worse than none; NOT built. The genuinely non-forgeable channel is the phone-signer HMAC (`record_director_ntfy_ruling`): it keys on `SE_WAKE_HMAC_KEY`, which this session verified is (a) ABSENT from the worker env, (b) only REFERENCED never valued anywhere in the working tree, (c) in `background/secrets_location.MODEL_FACING_FORBIDDEN_SECRETS` (scrubbed from every model-facing spawn env). A secret the worker cannot read is the real boundary. So the director's own contingency stands: the phone-signer setup is URGENT -- a console act per BUILD_OPEN reintroduces exactly the human dependency it removes, and the verified-commit trick cannot substitute. Primary state: gh auth status / gh api (session commands), background/secrets_location.py:40, background/gate_authorization.py (record_director_ntfy_ruling fail-closed), background/director_authority_channels.py.

58f8fa8364c2.question: Stall-set coverage verdict on the four events (console rescue, publish-gate wedge >1h, origin freeze >30m, advisor restart-ruling): detected / detector-added / argued-out?
58f8fa8364c2.disposition: ANSWERED (2026-07-28, per-event, evidence-cited): coverage is PARTIAL. (1) Console rescue -- NOT detected as an event; only its symptom is caught (deadmans_switch.py commit-cadence BLOCKED/STALL tiers fire when no meaningful commit lands within the window). The counter-reset it should trigger depends on the unbuilt exit-criterion counter (see Q2). (2) Publish-gate wedge >1h -- DETECTED: the wedge alert clears only on a successful publish (record_publish_gate_success) plus the eighth-class 2h age-cap on a blocked pending-batch. (3) Origin freeze >30m -- DETECTED (detector added after the incident): self-verifying push verifies ls-remote origin==HEAD; deadman keys on commits reaching origin. (4) Advisor restart-ruling -- NOT a machine detector by design: a policy reset condition (a staged doc doorbelling the machine awake resets the counter), enforced only by the unbuilt counter (Q2). Verdict: 2 of 4 have live detectors; the other 2 (console rescue, advisor-restart) are gated on building the exit-criterion counter. Primary state: background/deadmans_switch.py, d81197736 section 3.

a056615002f9.question: Staleness disposition in the gap taxonomy (27271871e section 3a).
a056615002f9.disposition: ANSWERED (2026-07-28 -- director-delegated 'your call', 27271871e section 3a): staleness is dispositioned as a READ-TIME FILTER in GAP1's reader contract, NOT a fifth bucket. Rationale: a stale row (superseded / already fixed / describes a removed component) is not a gap-category -- it is a data-quality condition on the row -- so a fifth bucket would break the four buckets' mutual-exclusion-over-LIVE-gaps and, under ambiguous-defaults-to-mint, manufacture work for a gap that no longer exists. The reader already verifies each row against primary state (LAW-C independent read); that is where staleness is detected. Evidence test: the row's primary-state referent no longer exists / is already closed -> the row is dropped before triage (not routed to a bucket). This is consistent with the fail-open fix already minted in PLANNER_MINTED_gap1_reader_contract_failopen_fix. Net: four buckets stay over live gaps; staleness is a pre-triage reader filter.

ded5e99d9b71.question: Blast radius as positive value versus risk (27271871e section 3b).
ded5e99d9b71.disposition: ANSWERED (2026-07-28 -- director-delegated, 27271871e section 3b): blast radius is DELIBERATELY FOLDED into value as a tie-breaker; risk is NOT scored separately. Honest basis (the ruling's own sanctioned disposition, 'if folded for simplicity, say so and leave it; not worth a mechanism'): for these gaps value and risk move together -- a gap touching many surfaces is both higher-value to fix and higher-risk to leave -- so a single blast-radius term serves both as the diagnostic tie-breaker. No separate risk axis exists in the ordering and none is warranted; left folded, no mechanism added. R12 respected: blast-radius is a tie-breaker diagnostic, never a target.

1b40d17f68ee.disposition: Same file's Done framed it in docs/design/CUSTOMER_NEEDS_BEYOND_THREE_CURRENCIES.md as seven needs, each with its own unit: cost, cash flow, certainty, control, time, carbon, and a comfort/health floor. af829b9bd63e.question: What about control?
af829b9bd63e.disposition: Yes. Control is a separate need under peace of mind (deciding when money leaves), measured apart from certainty. Framed in CUSTOMER_NEEDS_BEYOND_THREE_CURRENCIES.md and written into M3 by 83f5525c6f.

af352cf27c8f.question: Or cash low?
af352cf27c8f.disposition: Fragment of 'Or cash flow? Or is that part of money?'. Answered as both: money is two things measured apart, cost (what is paid) and cash flow (when, and how much at once). Framed in CUSTOMER_NEEDS_BEYOND_THREE_CURRENCIES.md and in amended M3 (83f5525c6f).

537d00738512.question: Or is that part of money?
537d00738512.disposition: Fragment of the same question: yes, cash flow is part of money but measured apart from cost. That is amended M3's 'Money is two things, measured apart' (83f5525c6f).

f77d0e89c266.question: I'm thinking why do some people pay more deliberately by cash or prepayment rather than have DD discount and smoothing?
f77d0e89c266.disposition: Same file's Done gives the GB evidence. In Ofgem's 2022 survey, 89% of DD, 85% of SC and 72% of PPM users give an active reason for their method. Control is SC payers' top reason and budgeting PPM payers', and only 55% know costs vary by method. Imposed PPM is a separate population (CUSTOMER_NEEDS_BEYOND_THREE_CURRENCIES.md; also docs/market_research/why_households_pay_the_way_they_do_cim_wave3_2026-11-02.md).

5f6977f9349b.question: Will the gas price have appropriate volatility too?
5f6977f9349b.disposition: Not yet. The K8 page (docs/market_research/how_gb_gas_and_power_prices_move_2026-10-25.md §0.1) finds the world's 'NBP' is a monthly-flat TTF proxy, so daily and weekly gas volatility is zero by construction (recorded as blocking in 085f89e42e). What would answer it: a daily NBP (or daily TTF plus FX) history (gap 9), volatility claims in tools/world_claims.py (none exist), and EP16 grading the generators against them. Carried on EP16 (forward-years grading against the volatility claims), which his 26 Oct correctness ruling holds behind the correctness stretch.

b847cb1a34a8.question: And mix and depth of backwardation and contango?
b847cb1a34a8.disposition: Not yet. The same page §0.2 finds the forward quote is an EWMA times a fixed monthly shape times an always-positive premium. Backwardation arises only from the shape or EWMA lag, and the seasonal spread cannot invert. The record's share of backwardated days is unpublished (gap 4). What would answer it: measure that share and the slope-on-spot from NBP and GB forward settlements, file it as a world claim, and grade the forward quote under EP16. Carried on EP16 (forward-years grading against the volatility claims), which his 26 Oct correctness ruling holds behind the correctness stretch.
